newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU adds to German barley, rye intvn export quota.
newsitem.headline: EU adds to German barley, rye intvn export quota.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday agreed to increase by another 300,000 tonnes the quota of German intervention barley available for export, grain traders said.
The EU's grain panel also agreed to add 150,000 tonnes to the allocation of German intervention rye available for export, they said.
Last Thursday the EU had already agreed to increase by 300,000 tonnes the quota of German intervention barley available for export.
The latest award brings to 1.1 million tonnes the total quota of German intervention barley set aside for export to non-EU destinations since the start of the 1996/97 campaign.
Earlier on Thursday the European Union sold around 183,000 tonnes of German intervention barley for export to non-EU destinations.
The grain is seen as mostly destined to help cover a large sale to Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia bought 800,000 tonnes of optional barley on August 21, traders have said.
Exporters had been pressing for an increase in the German barley export quota to help cover part of the sale.
